balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For The Star Entertainment Group Limited: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For The Star Entertainment Group Limited: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For The Star Entertainment Group Limited: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For The Star Entertainment Group Limited: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For The Star Entertainment Group Limited: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For The Star Entertainment Group Limited: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For The Star Entertainment Group Limited: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

propertyRevenue.title: Revenue by property
propertyRevenue.content:
Star operates three casino properties: The Star Sydney, The Star Gold Coast, and Brisbane, which is mid-handover from the old Treasury Brisbane casino to the new Queen's Wharf precinct (Star Brisbane), opened August 2024.

For The Star Entertainment Group: Sydney is the earnings engine and the one most exposed to the NSW regulator's ongoing supervision; Brisbane's revenue should shift from Treasury to Star Brisbane as the old casino closes, not simply add up -- a rising combined total while Star Brisbane ramps slower than Treasury declines is the handover failing to pay for itself.

What to watch:

  • Star Brisbane's ramp rate against Treasury Brisbane's decline
  • Sydney revenue trend as the carded-play and cashless-gaming mandates bite

propertyEbitda.title: Property EBITDA (Sydney vs Gold Coast)
propertyEbitda.content:
Earnings before corporate costs, interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation at the two mature properties -- the cleanest read on underlying trading since it strips out group-level regulatory and legal costs.

For The Star Entertainment Group: both properties' EBITDA fell in H1 FY2026 versus H1 FY2025 (Sydney $57.0m to $35.9m, Gold Coast $50.2m to $39.1m) -- the going-concern risk is as much a demand/regulatory-settings problem as a Brisbane-transition one.

What to watch:

  • Whether property EBITDA stabilises once carded-play and cashless-gaming mandates fully phase in
  • Gold Coast as the lower-regulatory-risk property, useful as a baseline for how much of the Sydney decline is regulation versus the broader gaming downturn

regulatoryCosts.title: Regulatory, legal and tax-settlement costs
regulatoryCosts.content:
Costs tied to the NSW Bell Inquiry and AUSTRAC AML/CTF enforcement -- remediation, legal fees, and penalties -- plus one-off tax dispute settlements, shown separately from normal operating costs because they explain most of the net losses since FY2023.

For The Star Entertainment Group: FY2023's $594.8m (including the NSW casino-licence suspension) was the peak; the decline to $20-25m by FY2025-FY2026 is the clearest signal that the acute regulatory crisis is past, even though the going-concern and refinancing overhang remains.

What to watch:

  • Whether this run-rate keeps falling toward a normal compliance-cost base
  • New AUSTRAC or state-regulator actions that would restart the cycle
  • One-off settlements (like FY2026's $55.9m tax dispute) distorting a single year's net income

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For The Star Entertainment Group Limited: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For The Star Entertainment Group Limited: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For The Star Entertainment Group Limited: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
